To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified and characterized a novel LTR retrotransposable element from P. westermania trematode parasite and its homologous elements in a mosquito species.

we have identified a new Ty3/gypsy LTR retrotransposable element from the human lung fluke, Paragonimus westermannii, and that the element has been differentially preserved in the host genome according to the host chromosomal ploidy.
the LTR retrotransposable elements of the trematode P. westermania have been identified and their mobile potentials are differentially maintained in association with host chromosomal polylploidy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolutionary history of LTR retroelements and their impact on genome evolution of parasitic helminthes.
the evolutionary pathway of LTR retroelements in the Platyhelminth and Insect genomes.
a novel LTR retrotransposition system in the trematodes and its evolutionary implication in association with chromosomal polyploidization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the LTR retrotransposition of the elements with the overlapped reading frame is a primitive state of evolution in which the ORFs are fused, and that the separate ORFs with the identical reading frame is the derived state, which is more advanced and complex.

the PwRn family of LTR retroelements, as a whole, has been preserved in the genome of P. westermania, while the individual elements have been maintained differentially, in association with host chromosomal polploidy.

the evolutionary history of CsRn-1 and its homologous elements in the trematodes and insects was likely to have been shaped by the interplay between their host genome structures and the mobile potential of retrotransposons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PwRn-like elements are likely to have been involved in the genome remodeling of the trematodes and the mosquito, and their evolutionary pathway may be associated with host karyotype.
the PwRn elements have been differentially preserved in host genomes according to chromosomal polyploidization.
the PwRn-like retrotransposons have evolved a diverse expression mechanism, which may be a consequence of their differentially preserved mobile potentials according to host genome structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mobile potential of retrotransposons is differentially preserved in association with host chromosomal polypeptides.

the LTR retrotransposition of PwR1 in P. westermannii is likely to have been differentially preserved according to the host chromosomal ploidy, which is a unique feature of this element among the known CsRn1-related retrotransposons.
a single element, such as PwRn, can be a powerful tool for understanding the evolutionary and functional roles of retrotransposons in the trematodes.
